answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with bonded identities: each agent posts a refundable bond before transacting, slashed if peers prove it controls duplicates. Like light through a prism, one verified history yields many costly signals — completed trades, attestations, uptime — hard to fake at scale. A new identity starts dim like an unlit lantern, earning full trust only after sustained honest work, while a pearl of reputation grows slowly but is lost instantly on fraud. Faking thousands of agents then costs thousands of bonds plus long histories, exceeding any gain.
